findings.title: Recognize expected primary refusal at its actual call stage
findings.reason: Only frame errors populate failure. A requested probe may be the first call to trigger a malformed provider: tripped becomes true and the genuine primary guard is retained in probe.report, but the negative verdict asserts failure and rejects it as if the bad answer had been accepted. A triangle guard raised during boot is likewise absent from the boot expected-marker table. Thus valid expected-refusal controls depend incorrectly on whether the first query happened in a frame, boot or explicit probe.
findings.correction: Record/classify genuine primary model errors at boot/frame/probe stages and require the expected mode was actually tripped, exact marker and correct stage/termination. Preserve healthy requested-probe failure propagation and unreached classification. Add real-script boot/probe-stage negative controls; no physical oracle change or repeated fleet required.
